None of the observed behavior is acceptable FMPOV. From what you describe, I see multiple issues we should probably address:

1. As you already mentioned, closing the connection also entails discarding of the registration assertion. Given the cost at which it needs to be created, one could ask whether it makes sense to close the connection at all once the adapter runs out of credits. On the other hand, closing the connection may trigger the client to (re-)connect to another adapter instance which hopefully has credits available.
1. The adapters currently assume that the registry is always available for issuing an assertion. However, IIRC the device registry just hands out 20 credits to an adapter for issuing requests. I think this will prove to be a bottleneck in the scenario described by you when hundreds of devices re-connect and send their first message. We should probably take precautions in the adapters to refuse messages if there are no credits available for requesting assertions from the Device Registration service.

In any case, your expectation regarding the system remaining in a stable state and degrading gracefully is more than appropriate.

Should this be MIN_MODULE_VERSION_SYSTEM_PART2 instead of SYSTEM_MODULE_VERSION_0_7_0_RC1?

[2017-06-07T22:34:40Z | sergeuz | review_comment]
> Should this be MIN_MODULE_VERSION_SYSTEM_PART2 instead of SYSTEM_MODULE_VERSION_0_7_0_RC1?

No, `MIN_MODULE_VERSION_SYSTEM_PART2` is internal for `bootloader_dct.c`.

> Also should module_ver be declared as const int16_t to match return sign from get_main_module_version()?

Yeah, `module_ver` should be a signed integer, thanks. I first used 0 as error code, but then it appeared that 0 is actually used as a version number for all current monolithic builds.

> Part of this question is correct logic, and other part what should the default be in case of module corruption? Seems like we'd need to disable the IWDG to be able to DFU new firmware, so we'd want to always default to IWDG disabled.

This code actually doesn't check integrity of any system modules, it only checks version of the main system module (which is either part2 or monolithic firmware module) to workaround particular issue with downgrading from 0.7.0. There's an existing logic in the bootloader, which turns the device into DFU mode once a specific number of IWDG resets is reached, though I never seen it in action.

[2017-06-07T22:49:06Z | technobly | review_comment]
Re: corrupted module, worst case example: if a module was simply and completely erased, would `get_main_module_version()` return -1?  Basically if the module header is corrupted/erased, will get_module_info() return NULL?  I guess it's also possible that the header is corrupted and get_main_module_version() returns something > 200 by mistake.

[2017-06-07T23:14:45Z | sergeuz | review_comment]
Right, `get_module_info()` (and thus `get_main_module_version()`) returns data straight from the module's header on flash, so if the header is corrupted in a weird way it's possible that the IWDG won't be enabled. We can add an integrity check here, but I'd like to ensure that it won't affect the boot time. There's a similar check already, which is performed when DCT functions are loaded, but it doesn't happen on every boot, only on demand.

[2017-06-07T23:40:20Z | technobly | review_comment]
@sergeuz Can we bound it also to the current SYSTEM_PART1_MODULE_VERSION, so if the header was corrupt and greater than SYSTEM_PART1_MODULE_VERSION (at the time bootloader was compiled), it would disable the IWDG as well.  That might mean updating to a new system firmware would disable the IWDG though... hmm, how about just giving it some kind of sane upper bounds for the time being like (SYSTEM_PART1_MODULE_VERSION + 500) to allow for some upgrade buffer but still protect against 99% of corrupt values `((65536-500)/65536)*100`.  If nothing else, we could protect against the erased state (0xFFFF) if that doesn't result in get_module_info() returning NULL but instead returning 65535 for `module_ver`.

[2017-06-08T00:09:54Z | sergeuz | review_comment]
It's the opposite: we don't want to enable IWDG for module versions < 200 (0.7.0-rc.1), since older firmwares won't be able detect if IWDG is running. In other words, we're enabling IWDG for any firmware version in the range 200-65535, which includes most of the potentially corrupted values and erased state.

[2017-06-08T00:17:30Z | technobly | review_comment]
Ah true, and in that case the bootloader will end up in DFU mode after a few tries and resets due to IWDG, yeah?

[2017-06-08T00:30:38Z | sergeuz | review_comment]
Yep. Ideally, bootloader should always check integrity of a newly flashed firmware with all its dependencies, and then save a flag to the DCT to avoid checking it until next update. This will allow bootloader to enter DFU mode instantly in case of a corrupted firmware, without relying on IWDG (which, in turn, ideally should be kept enabled all the time).

Yes, I think I know what the problem is here:

1. There indeed was a conscious decision to also inform the handler about an update as soon as the `initialize()` method returned. The assumption is the even if the Thing is not yet in ONLINE/OFFLINE/UNKNOWN status, the ThingHandler still started doing something, hence also needs to be informed if something changed.  You are right, the documentation needs to be updated. We missed that. 

2. There was another change in the ThingManager which made the `initialize()` be called asynchronously. As it seems, this broke the "protection" described above, so that `thingUpdated()` currently also can get called while the `initialize()` is still running. This is a bug and needs to be fixed somehow. 

It's all a bit tricky, therefore I can't promise to fix it immediately, but I will have a look into this in the next couple of days.

[2017-07-06T12:53:21Z | AndWass | comment]
Found a fix you might want to try as well.

In message_sender.c in function on_link_state_changed a call will be made to the function `indicate_all_messages_as_error`. This function frees all the messages and their associated memory. After this (a little while on) `on_session_state_changed` (in link.c) will be called with the new state set to SESSION_STATE_ERROR. This will call `remove_all_pending_deliveries` which will loop through all pending deliveries and call the `on_delivery_settled callback`. This callback will then touch and attempt to use the previously freed memory and finally also free the message again.

Simply removing all calls to `indicate_all_messages_as_error` in `on_link_state_change` (around lines 560 in message_sender.c in uamqp) will make the crashing go away but I don't know if this causes other problems though.

[2019-08-30T05:33:26Z | calohmn | comment]
Adding some further debug output has revealed that the `Rejected` disposition has the error "Deliveries cannot be sent to an unavailable address":
````
Rejected{error=Error{condition=amqp:not-found, description='Deliveries cannot be sent to an unavailable address', info=null}
````
(I've improved log output since to always reveal this, see https://github.com/eclipse/hono/commit/7aa91cd29f3d16d0f28033c3de3bade16e09b753.)

What seemingly happened here:
The DelegatedCommandSenderImpl that forwards the received command on the device-specific command address uses a sender link on the *anonymous relay* (so that one link can be used for multiple tenants/devices).
That means the sender doesn't get credits for the particular address to be used here and so it isn't assured that there actually is a receiver for the device-specific command address.
The Qpid error message above indicates just that; no receiver on that address was available.

At first sight, this doesn't seem possible, because we always create a device-specific command receiver link *first*, before the application gets the indication that a device can receive a command.
But here the fact comes into play that a network of multiple Qpid dispatch router instances is used in this case.

So, the steps were:
The receiver link gets created in connection with Qpid instance A.
Then the command message should get sent on the anonymous relay in connection with Qpid instance B.
The information about the receiver link wasn't propagated in the router network to Qpid instance B yet, so an "unavailable address" is returned.

See also [this discussion](http://qpid.2158936.n2.nabble.com/Dispatch-Router-Anon-relay-sender-link-rejected-msgs-timing-issue-td7685763.html) on the Qpid list on this.

[2019-08-30T09:40:14Z | calohmn | comment]
To fix this, I see these options:
1. Insert a delay *after* creating the device-specific command consumer link and *before* informing the application about the fact that the device can receive commands. During this delay, the information about the attached receiver is supposed to be propagated in the router network, so that when sending the command message on the anonymous relay link, the message gets accepted (hopefully). 
1. Use a sender link with the device-specific command address (instead of using the anonymous relay). In case the received command has to be forwarded via the DelegatedCommandSenderImpl, the sender link is opened, the command message is sent and then the link is closed.
1. Use the current solution (with anonymous relay link) and do retries if sending the command message failed with the above error.

With solution 1, the question is how to choose a delay that is small enough not to delay the whole command processing too much (could be noticable especially in the HTTP case) but large enough to ensure qpid has propagated the receiver info to all instances.

With solution 3, the question is which delay period and which number of retries to choose.

I would prefer solution 2 here. I would rather have the (I guess small) overhead of creating the link each time instead of having to deal with delays or retries.

The issue arises when the queuebuf is (almost) full. Packets are fragmented, but there are not enough buffer available for all the fragments and the last fragments are dropped. However the fragmentation code does not remove the already scheduled fragments. So, in the end, only the first fragment of all packets is sent.

Solution is to check if enough buffers are available for all the fragments before starting the fragmentation mechanism. (And also increases the amount of available buffers)

Summarizing the discussion from IRC:

Currently there is the problem that, on the request/response service side, there is no correlation between the receiver of the request and the sender of the response. So it isn't possible to do proper credit tracking.

My proposal would be to re-structure the request/response functionality in a way that is uses the EventBus reply feature and use that as a way to send the response to the requestor. This also seems to appropriate way to use the EventBus from a vertx point of view.

For this to work, it is required though to know to which link to send the response to. For this, an in-memory map will be added, which records which senders are registered for each reply-to address.

This change would also eliminate the need the an explicit call to `consume` on the event bus, and thus resolves the memory leak described in #753.

[2018-08-06T11:00:19Z | sophokles73 | comment]
> For this to work, it is required though to know to which link to send the response to. For this, an in-memory map will be added, which records which senders are registered for each reply-to address.
This change would also eliminate the need the an explicit call to consume on the event bus, and thus resolves the memory leak described in #753.

I agree that this will prevent EventBusConsumers to leak in the situation described in #753. However, it will introduce another potential leak: when a client breaks away, we still need to make sure that the sender gets removed from the map. So, in any case we need to deal with clients breaking away unexpectedly.

I would therefore rather stick with the current implementation in order to not turn everything upside down (again), add the *sender/reply-to* map and make sure that we both close the corresponding EventBusConsumer and remove the sender from the map when a client disconnects (unexpectedly). The map can then be used to flow credit to the sender when a response message has been received from the event bus.

[2018-06-08T16:57:09Z | avranju | comment]
The fix for this issue is under review right now. This will work when Azure IoT Edge becomes generally available. You'll be able to specify the network configuration via "create options" in the deployment and Edge Agent will honor that setting and not try to add the container to the bridged network. The flip side of this change is that the container loses the ability to access other modules in the deployment directly by name, i.e., module names no longer resolve to their container IP addresses since the container which is on the host network is not part of the bridged network. Modules that wish to be accessible from the host network can achieve that by port mapping the container port to a host port.

[2018-06-28T01:28:14Z | avranju | comment]

[2020-03-12T21:33:34Z | arsing | comment]
Windows does not support `host` networking, as documented by Docker at https://docs.docker.com/network/host/ So it's expected that it won't work, and is not related to IoT Edge.

Now, as documented at https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/virtualization/windowscontainers/container-networking/network-drivers-topologies , you could create a new Docker network yourself using the `transparent` driver. If you then set that network name to be the value of `moby_runtime.network` in `config.yaml`, all your modules would be started on this network instead of the default `nat` network.

However, Moby on Windows has another bug where any non-built-in networks become unusable after a reboot. This is because they get a new ID but all containers remain associated with the old ID, so they don't start. The only mitigation is to delete all containers and let them be recreated, so that they attach to the new ID. This bug is also why IoT Edge itself does not default to using the `azure-iot-edge` network on Windows like on Linux, and instead uses the built-in `nat` network. I suspect that any network you create manually would have the same problem.

If the network you create *does* have that problem, then you will need to follow up with https://github.com/moby/moby/issues

Since the Elasticsearch rest client is widely used by the comunity we are introducing the rest client support in the Kapua datastore feature.

[2016-07-11T16:27:15Z | tekka007 | comment]
Thanks for reporting. 
Defining `MY_PARENT_NODE_ID` sets a _preferred_ parent for routing/forwarding messages, if the parent is offline or not responding, the fallback mechanism kicks in and searches for a new (active) parent. 
Setting `MY_PARENT_NODE_IS_STATIC` should override this behavior and prevent parent node searching and reassignment, this seems not to be the case and requires further investigations.

[2016-01-27T13:31:00Z | dvanherbergen | comment]
This is what appears to be happening:

The bundle org.eclipse.smarthome.core.transform is being started. This bundle provides a service which implements org.eclipse.smarthome.model.script.engine.action.ActionService. That interface class is located in the bundle org.eclipse.smarthome.model.script, which has been configured to start when one of its classes are loaded, so the loading of this interface class triggers the start of the org.eclipse.smarthome.model.script bundle.
In the activator of this bundle, it tries to open a service tracker on ActionService services, but this returns null, probably because the service org.eclipse.smarthome.core.transform is still being started.

[2017-01-10T13:19:40Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> Before I break bazillions of SmartHome solutions

You are standing a good chance to do so ;-)

> any good reason for the states NOT being transformed at those two places (i.e. rest/items/.../state and in the Events)?

They simply provide the REAL item state, i.e. the full truth. Note that item states are for "headless" use, i.e. not UI related at all.

When defining an item like

```
Contact Wohnzimmer_Fenster1_OpenClosed  "Wohnzimmerfenster 1 [MAP(de.map):%s]" 
```

you have to note that the part in quotes specifies a "default label" to use, if no other label is specified in a UI. So while there is one single state of the item, it might have many different visual representations depending on its usage. That's why the sitemap endpoint provides the mapped state (but note that you could have specified the mapping in the sitemap as well and this could be a different one than the default given in the item file).

If you're talking about rebuilding everything including dependencies, there's a flag in the latest build script for that: `--rebuild-deps`.

[2020-01-31T10:13:44Z | calohmn | comment]
We were able to reproduce the above exception in a load-test environment, creating many links, and also in a small test class.
The issue occurs when Hono throws a "link establishment timed out" exception and subsequently closes the link and also calls "link.free()" to free up ressources, *and* when the server still responds with an "attach" frame afterwards, before finally sending a "detach".

There is now this Proton-J issue for that: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/PROTON-2177

Solution/workaround would to omit calling "link.free()" on linkEstablishmentTimeout handling, hoping that the server will finally respond with a "detach" frame after which we then can call "link.free()".

I'll update the PR accordingly.

[2016-01-20T12:13:40Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
I found the problem, it is after all in the NTP binding:
If an existing thing is re-discovered, updated configuration from the discovery result is automatically sync'ed to the thing. As the NTP discovery set the default values, this overwrote any changes upon a rediscovery (which was automatically triggered at system startup).
I have removed this now in the NtpDiscovery in #894

The registry content is updated accordingly. This is all what is to be expected of it - it holds the rules and allows their modification.

Anybody who is interested in rules (like the rule engine) should register as a `RegistryChangeListener` on the RuleRegistry and will be notified of any changes and can react to it.

[2017-07-27T10:07:59Z | danchom | comment]
>Anybody who is interested in rules (like the rule engine) should register as a RegistryChangeListener on the RuleRegistry and will be notified of any changes and can react to it.

yes this will be done, but I mean the following problems:
1) RuleRegistry is used as public API for RuleEngine. (only through this api you can have influence to the rule engine). Unfortunately there are other public method which are not covered by the  RegistryChangeListener  i.e. isEnable(), setEnable(), runNow(). We have to introduce RuleEngineComandCallback interface to notify the RuleEngine about the actions. The other approach is the RuleEngine component to export its own public interface which will have to support these operation, but in this case we will have again the cycle dependency :
RuleEngine -> RuleRegistry  for add, update, remove 
RuleRegistry -> RuleEngine for setEnable, isEnable and runNow
2) When a user add a rule into RuleRegistry he won't know if the rule is running by the rule engine or not. At the moment if the rule is added into ruleRegistry it is a guarantee  that it is process by the RuleEngine.

[2017-07-27T11:25:13Z | kaikreuzer | comment]

@abhatikar I reproduced the issue you're seeing (you're on Pi, I'm on a Docker Ubuntu 16.04 container, but same error). Here's how I encountered it:

```bash
apt-get install -y nodejs npm nodejs-legacy # installs v4.2.6
git clone https://github.com/azure/iot-edge.git
cd iot-edge
tools/build.sh --enable-nodejs-remote-modules # produces the original error for this GitHub issue
curl -sL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_8.x | bash -
apt-get install -y nodejs # installs v8.0.0
tools/build.sh --enable-nodejs-remote-modules # produces your error, in the nanomsg binding
```
I fixed the problem by cleaning the repo before building again:
```
git clean -xdf .
tools/build.sh --enable-nodejs-remote-modules # build succeeds
```
I think your error was just some weird interaction between the old and new versions of Node.js. Specifically, the `nanomsg` module uses node-gyp to build its underlying C library, and I'm pretty sure C interop is not compatible between major versions of Node.js. So using nanomsg built from an older version of Node.js isn't guaranteed to work. Deleting the `proxy/gateway/nodejs/node_modules/` folder forces everything to rebuild, and then it works.

Can you trying cleaning/rebuilding the iot-edge code, as I did above?

[2017-06-08T22:26:20Z | damonbarry | comment]
@camauser The following command in the build script:
```
CORES2=$(expr ${MEMAR[0]} / 500000)
```
Evaluates to this in your environment:
```
expr 498380 / 500000
```
...which returns the value `0`. That's all fine, except that the _exit status_ of the `expr` command in this case is non-zero, so the `set -e` command at the top of the script causes the script to exit.

Since we care about the expression result and not the exit status of `expr`, I've made a pull request that causes the script to disregard the exit status of this particular command.

[2019-02-11T06:20:59Z | LeoNerdoG | comment]
Hi Alberto,
If we look at the setting in Child Accounts -> Account Settings -> CredentialService there is setting called "lockoutPolicy.maxFailures" and the description of this setting is: "Number of consecutive login failures before the user gets locked. Valid if lockout policy is enabled."

This description is the reason I opened this issue. There is a certain similarity with entering PIN number when you go to ATM. You get 3 shots at entering the right PIN. If you miss three times, you do not get another shot, because you have already used all the tries and ATM would give you error message after the forth try, even if it is the right combination. 

It is similar here - after third try user does not get the message that he is locked out, but rather that enterd password is not correct. He then gets another try and if he enters right password this time, it is no use - Kapua would throw "locked out" error message in any case. 

So I see two different solutions now - either we throw "user locked" error message after 3rd try (if "lockoutPolicy.maxFailures" is set to 3 - as it is logical to inform user that he is locked after the las valid attempt) or we change the description of the setting to be more informational. 

Leonardo

[2018-03-13T14:30:08Z | sjsf | comment]
I did a little further analysis. There are two options:

a)
the thing handler _was_ successfully initialized before because it could handle the missing bridge situation gracefully and went ONLINE. Then the bridge handler is _not_ informed _correctly_ as the child handle won't be initialized again. It gets informed about the updated thing instead. All good, works a designed.

b)
the thing handle failed during the initialize and threw an exception, the thing went into `UNINITIALIZED/HANDLER_INITIALIZING_ERROR`. In this case, the framework attempts to initialize the handler. However, there is glitch in there - the handler was created before with the "old" thing, and therefore we  run into this situation:

https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/blob/ec3cc58a493da1293c166513928ce92b8c85eeff/bundles/core/org.eclipse.smarthome.core.thing/src/main/java/org/eclipse/smarthome/core/thing/internal/ThingManager.java#L571-L574

As a result, the thing manager updates the wrong thing and the thing handler keeps operating on the old thing.

[2020-03-02T20:24:32Z | technobly | review_comment]
My suggestion here is if we see multiple values, to leave the RSRP and RSRQ as their last known value.  If we read multiple values for a second time, then perhaps we should set the values to one that indicates an error since we don't trust the readings any longer.  One problem with this approach is we don't currently control the retry interval.  A user could be calling Particle.publishVitals() every 1 second, or maybe every 30s.  So that persisted value could hang around for much longer than it should.

Another approach would be to force one retry in Device OS after a delay of 300ms if the first read contained multiple values.  This might not be long enough for the tower hand off to have occurred though, so some characterization may need to be done here with mobile testing.  One possible negative affect to this approach is occasionally the Particle.publishVitals() API will block for a bit longer while it tries to resolve this issue.

The reason why I like this approach is because in practice when mobile testing, when I would see multiple values reported for RSRP and RSRQ, I would still be able to publish data and it was received by the server.  So if we ultimately will be using RSRP and RSRQ to help qualify network operations (publishes, etc..), I would like to avoid being overly cautious and optimize for being overly optimistic (due to previous testing).  Reason being, if we can't send certain messages due to being overly cautious, it can cause an even longer delay while we tear down the network connection and rebuild it.

Without having an explicit interpretation of what multiple responses means, we must characterize it and implement a strategy for interpreting it that best suits our customers.

[2016-06-14T14:45:08Z | R-Edelhoff | comment]
Yes i can reproduce the issue with following steps:
- Sonos player will be paired while reachable in network -> State of created thing is ONLINE
- Restart the runtime and disconnect the Sonos device afterwards
- When the runtime is back again the state of the thing is still ONLINE 

The rootcause for this issue is that the polling runnable (where the thing state is periodically updated)
will not be scheduled when the ThingHandler gets initialized. This happens because the UpnpIOParticipant (which is the ZonePlayerHandler in this case) is not registered to the UpnpIOService at this time and the "isRegistered()" check prevents the handler to schedule the runnable during initialization.

However the "isRegistered()" is not required at this point because the UpnpIOParticipant will anyway be registered (if not already done) when using the UpnpIOService in the following calls of "addSubscription()" and "*.invokeAction()". Hence we can remove this check which is fixing the issue and does not create any regression as i have tested as well.

I will not going to set the thing status to OFFLINE after initialization because the Thing state will appear as OFFLINE for 60s after pairing the device which is confusing. We rather need to make sure that the polling runnable will always be scheduled to enforce a thing status update within max. 60s.

Hi, there. This is my code I use for the v1 motor shield, controlled by a Spark:

``` javascript
var Cylon = require('cylon');

Cylon.robot({
  connection: {
    name: 'spark', adaptor: 'spark',
    accessToken: '[your access token]',
    deviceId: '[your device id]'
  },

  devices: [
  {name: 'leftMotor', driver: 'motor', pin: "D1"},
  {name: 'rightMotor', driver: 'motor', pin: "A7"},
  {name: 'leftDirection', driver: 'direct-pin', pin: "D3"},
  {name: 'rightDirection', driver: 'direct-pin', pin: "D4"}
  ],

  work: function(my) {
    my.leftDirection.digitalWrite(1);
    my.rightDirection.digitalWrite(1);
    my.leftMotor.speed(100);
    my.rightMotor.speed(100);
    after((10).seconds(), function() {
      my.leftDirection.digitalWrite(0);
      my.rightDirection.digitalWrite(0);
    });
    after((20).seconds(), function() {
      my.leftDirection.digitalWrite(1);
      my.rightDirection.digitalWrite(0);
    });
    after((21).seconds(), function() {
      my.leftDirection.digitalWrite(0);
      my.rightDirection.digitalWrite(1);
    });
    after((22).seconds(), function() {
      my.leftDirection.digitalWrite(1);
      my.rightDirection.digitalWrite(0);
    });
    after((23).seconds(), function() {
      my.leftDirection.digitalWrite(0);
      my.rightDirection.digitalWrite(1);
    });
    after((24).seconds(), function() {
      my.leftMotor.turnOff();
      my.rightMotor.turnOff();
    });
  }
}).start();
```

The v1 motor shield uses 2 pins per motor that it can control. One PWM for speed, the other for direction.

Hope that helps!

[2017-05-02T07:19:40Z | htreu | comment]
Here are my findings regarding the loss of SSE connection during/after extension install:

The problem occurs only on extensions which extend the REST API of ESH. During install/uninstall of these extensions the OSGi JAX RS bridge ([found here](https://github.com/hstaudacher/osgi-jax-rs-connector/blob/master/bundles/com.eclipsesource.jaxrs.publisher/src/com/eclipsesource/jaxrs/publisher/internal/ServletContainerBridge.java)) recognises a change in REST resource configuration and   calls `reload` on the underlying ServletContainer (find sources [here](https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/glassfish/jersey/containers/jersey-container-servlet-core/2.22.1/)). ServletContainer#reload will then shutdown the ApplicationHandler (which handles all requests and also serves as a ContainerLifecycleListener for all resources, sources [here](https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/glassfish/jersey/core/jersey-server/2.22.1/)) and create a new ApplicationHandler with the changed resource config.

I assume the effect we are seeing here is a race condition between the SSE thread and the OSGI JAX RS bridge. Sometimes the SSE comes first and is able to provide feedback to the UI. Nevertheless will the SSE connection be broken after the ServletContainer reloads all resources.

[2017-06-10T00:48:46Z | jebrando | comment]
Ok, I believe I know what's going on.  The OS does not signal that the network is down to the app on a socket level, so the sdk thinks that it is successfully sending the message.  The SDK does not send MQTT keepAlive message since normal publish messages are being sent every few seconds, so it does not detect the a missed PINGRESP.  There is a few ways to fix this, and I'll discuss with product owners how they would like to see this resolved.

As far as the reconnect is concerned I believe that the network is in a bad state and fixing the first issue should resolve the reconnect.  I will talk to the correct people and report back.

Cheers.
Jelani

[2019-01-29T17:13:07Z | sophokles73 | review_comment]
it is true that the behavior in vertx-proton has changed. However, `ProtonSaslClientAuthenticatorImpl` uses different exceptions to indicate different types of failures:
```
  private void handleSaslFail() throws SaslException {
    switch(sasl.getOutcome()) {
    case PN_SASL_AUTH:
      throw new AuthenticationException("Failed to authenticate");
    case PN_SASL_SYS:
    case PN_SASL_TEMP:
      throw new SaslSystemException(false, "SASL handshake failed due to a transient error");
    case PN_SASL_PERM:
      throw new SaslSystemException(true, "SASL handshake failed due to an unrecoverable error");
    default:
      throw new SaslException("SASL handshake failed");
    }
  }
```
In particular, the most probable cause for failure (wrong credentials) is indicated by a `javax.security.sasl.AuthenticationException` (a subclass of `javax.security.sasl.SaslException`).

So, I think that we should catch `javax.security.sasl.SaslException` here instead of `SecurityException` and add another catch clause for `SaslSystemException` which is used to indicate cases where the server is not ready to process the handshake and fail with a `ServerErrorException` in that case.

* Fill module.json with the actual value of image registry
* Update .env to include credential entries for the new image registry

Okay. When you first install the GrovePi, you are also required to reboot the Pi. Only then you can start interfacing with it. (I haven't looked over your logs yet).

[2019-08-07T21:09:08Z | RobertLucian | comment]
The error you are getting on wxgtk2.8 is normal on the Buster image. This package is required for the GUI interface which I think you don't need, which means you can bypass the installation of it by running:
```
curl -kL dexterindustries.com/update_grovepi | bash -s -- --bypass-gui-installation
```

Either way, there's a fix out there in the pipeline for wxgtk2.8, but we haven't merged it yet because we need to test it. 

Truth to be told, we don't support any of our robots (or devices) on Buster/Pi4 because this distribution is still very buggy and because we're still working on making everything work smoothly. It's in the pipeline, but it's gonna take a bit more time until it's ready.

> I'd assume that they are even started because findEntries is using their ClassLoader.
> it heavily messes with bundle states before the framework actually resolves them properly and fixes the package wiring

I don't agree with these arguments. findEntries will not cause a bundle to be started; the worst thing that can happen is that an attempt to resolve a bundle will fail because of missing dependencies. Logs like the one in this issue are the result of errors in the bundles, or strange coincidences (automation tries to resolve a bundle, this sends resolved event for this or some other bundle, then a different bundle tracker calls getHeaders on this newly resolved bundles, which causes the exception) - and I don't think such rare cases should drive the requirements for the module

> if a bundle is not resolvable, there is a reason for that and most likely its other content (i.e. the automation resources) does not make sense in that situation either.

I can agree with this argument, but we have to be aware that resolving does not happen automatically:
- Bundle that contains only resources will never be resolved without explicitly starting or resolving it.
- Fragment bundle, installed after the host also will never be resolved without explicitly invoking "refresh packages".

This requires additional actions from the user and can lead to confusions. Are you sure you want to proceed with this change?

> I managed to get neopixelall to work, but neopixel is unrecognised and neopixelline - first use - say starting at 2 and ending at pixel 4 works but subsequent changes don't. Is this only partly implemented or am I missing something?

This three commands are implemented in Neopixel plugin:
NeoPixel,[led nr],[red 0-255],[green 0-255],[blue 0-255],[brightness 0-255]
NeoPixelAll,[red 0-255],[green 0-255],[blue 0-255],[brightness 0-255]
NeoPixelLine,[start led nr],[stop led nr],[red 0-255],[green 0-255],[blue 0-255],[brightness 0-255]

In NeoPixel command there are only two condition that makes it silently refuse to work: 1. HPWM compatible pin is not selected in the plugin, 2. LED number in command greater or equal than setted max LED count number. (led number is zero based) If NeoPixelAll works for all 12 LEDs than maybe some other error occurs.
On other errors RPIEasy writes them on the error log, do you see anything in the error log? Please add the content of the Log and the exact command lines in case of error.

[2019-05-21T18:38:44Z | YoDaMa | comment]
Just adding here. The uint16_t vs. tickcounter_ms_t is intentional. The documentation should be updated to indicate that tickcounter_ms_t is the necessary unit from the API side for setting this variable. It can also be added to the convenience sample to indicate the proper usage of this variable.

Your analysis on the code is good though (really, a great issue file with good code snippet and everything! Thanks!). Here's a deeper explanation:

**Why use `tickcounter_ms_t` for OPTION_DO_WORK_FREQUENCY_IN_MS?**
- In `iothub_client_core.c` the OPTION_DO_WORK_FREQUENCY_IN_MS has a value that is checked against `iotHubClientInstance->currentMessageTimeout`, which is of type `tickcounter_ms_t` (which is defined in the azure_c_shared_utilities as `uint_fast64_t` or `uint_fast32_t` depending on the platform). 
- Because of this check against `currentMessageTimeout`, OPTION_DO_WORK_FREQUENCY_IN_MS needs to be of a type `tickcounter_ms_t *`. 

**But then in `iothub_client_core.c`, `do_work_freq_ms` is set as a `uint16_t`. Why?**
- `do_work_freq_ms` is used to specify a sleep interval via `ThreadAPI_Sleep`, which takes a type `unsigned int`. 
- If the `do_work_freq_ms` were a `tickcounter_ms_t`, we end up with a bug. When it is cast to a `unsigned int` to input into `ThreadAPI_Sleep`, the number will be undefined (just random garbage). 
- So to avoid this we cast the `tickcounter_ms_t` pointer to a `uint16_t` pointer, and because we've set the range to be between 0-100, there's no chance of this pointer cast losing data. The `do_work_freq_ms` variable for `iotHubClientInstance` will be set as the dereferenced `uint16_t` pointer.

[2018-10-24T08:42:37Z | lorthirk | comment]
After some investigation I think I found the root cause. It's not about downloading Jetty, but the startup of Jetty itself is failing:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Cannot read file: modules/alpn-impl/alpn-1.8.0_191.mod
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Modules.registerModule(Modules.java:202)
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Modules.enable(Modules.java:355)
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Modules.enable(Modules.java:360)
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Modules.enable(Modules.java:377)
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Modules.enable(Modules.java:377)
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Modules.enable(Modules.java:286)
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.BaseBuilder.build(BaseBuilder.java:129)
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Main.start(Main.java:435)
	at org.eclipse.jetty.start.Main.main(Main.java:77)

Usage: java -jar $JETTY_HOME/start.jar [options] [properties] [configs]
       java -jar $JETTY_HOME/start.jar --help  # for more information
```

This happens because OpenJDK has been upgraded on yum, the CentOS repository manager. Now the latest available version is 1.8.0_191, but Jetty has no related ALPN module among its modules. I'm going to file a new issue in Jetty; in the meanwhile we could fix it with a workaround:

```
ln -s /opt/jetty/modules/alpn-impl/alpn-1.8.0_181.mod /opt/jetty/modules/alpn-impl/alpn-1.8.0_191.mod
```
since `alpn-1.8.0_181.mod` is the latest ALPN module in Jetty.

The problem is that our scheduler calculates the milliseconds until the next execution and in the cases of the bug that I am fixing the scheduler and the system time are a few (milli)seconds off and thus the expression scheduled to be executed at 0h 0m 0s is executed before midnight which is the day before. And in case of the Astro binding we are only interested in the day and not not the actual time of the cron execution.

If a cron expression that is using "00:00:00" as execution trigger is executed on the old day, I would say this is an unexpected behavior.

Changing the trigger cron expression will mask the error but not really solve the bug.

[2017-08-28T11:12:55Z | triller-telekom | comment]
Indeed you are right. Thanks for the report. I'm going to investigate on this.

However, about the last two points: it's actually by design that a user cannot change its own Settings, but rather a user from the parent account should be the one entitled to change them via the Child Accounts --> Settings view. [2017-11-09T17:31:36Z | ewertons | comment]
@davidbuechi , the frequency with which IoTHubClient_LL_DoWork is called depends on several factors, the top being how reliable a network is and how powerful the host device is.

Within the threaded layer of the Azure IoT C SDK (iothub_client.c), we call IoTHubClient_LL_DoWork every 1 millisecond. That in general is safe, but a little more frequent than most environments would require. Calling it once every second might be too slow for unreliable networks.

We would recommend you calling IoTHubClient_LL_DoWork every 10 to 100 milliseconds to be safe.

Hi @kaizimmerm,
I just repoduced this by creating a Service Bus instance and connecting to it using the Qpid JMS Client (the client we use in Ditto for connections to AMQP 1.0 brokers). I traced the communication between client and server, the service bus sets an idle timeout of 240000ms in the open frame. This value is interpreted by the Qpid JMS client and it would send a PING to keep the connection open after 120000ms ("remote idle timeout" / 2). Unfortunately the connection is closed after 60s by the link tracker:
> The connection was inactive for more than the allowed 60000 milliseconds and is closed by container 'LinkTracker'

So it seems that the Service Bus does not respect the idle timeout set by itself. I can provide a simple reproducer if required. The issue was however already reported but closed as expected behavior: https://github.com/Azure/azure-service-bus-java/issues/142 and https://github.com/Azure/azure-service-bus-java/issues/280

[2017-06-27T11:12:57Z | sophokles73 | comment]
The `HonoClient.connect(ProtonClientOptions, Handler, Handler)` variant provides a way to supply your own *disconnect handler*, which is invoked when the connection unexpectedly fails. You can provide a handler which basically invokes `HonoClient.connect()` again using the original *connection handler*.

The current API does not make any claims for the original *connection handler* being invoked again after a re-connect has occurred. I am not sure if this what a client would want to happen in the first place. That's what the variant of `HonoClient.connect()` mentioned above is intended to be used for ...

[2017-06-27T12:06:03Z | calohmn | comment]
> The HonoClient.connect(ProtonClientOptions, Handler, Handler) variant provides a way to supply your own disconnect handler, which is invoked when the connection unexpectedly fails. You can provide a handler which basically invokes HonoClient.connect() again using the original connection handler.

Yes, that is what we did and what is also done in `org.eclipse.hono.example.ExampleReceiver`.

> The current API does not make any claims for the original connection handler being invoked again after a re-connect has occurred. I am not sure if this what a client would want to happen in the first place.

What we want and what I guess is the most common scenario, is a consumer application that still gets telemetry messages and events after the connection to the Dispatch Router got lost several times. This means being able to ensure that `honoClient.createTelemetryConsumer()` is invoked after a re-connect. 

For the HonoClient to support this, I think it should either invoke the _connection handler_ on a re-connect, or the `HonoClient` API should support an extra _re-connect handler_.

```
astro:sun:home   [ geolocation="44.4444, 11.1111", interval=300 ] {
	Channels:
		Type rangeEvent : night#event [
			earliest="21:30",
			latest="22:30"
		]
		Type rangeEvent : night#event [
			earliest="06:00",
			latest="06:30"
		]
		Type rangeEvent : daylight#event [
			earliest="06:00",
			latest="07:30"
		]
		Type rangeEvent : daylight#event [
			earliest="16:00",
			latest="21:30"
		]
}
```

[2016-10-05T17:09:11Z | adarazs | comment]
Thank you for acknowledging the bug, I mean behavior. :)

I think it's clear for you at this point but just stating that this also affects dimmer types too, not just switches.

For others fighting with the same problem, my workaround is:
- remove the hue link from the switch item
- add a rule that updates the switch items periodically directly from the "color" type items like this:

``` java
// for color lights
postUpdate(living_light_ceiling_switch, if(living_light_ceiling_color.state.toString.split(",").get(2) == "0") OFF else ON)
// for dimmer only lights
postUpdate(dress_light_switch, if(dress_light_dimmer.state.toString == "0") OFF else ON)
```

Now the switch items are actually updated properly to their ON/OFF state and can be used in rules, but cannot be used to control the lights (use the color or dimmer items instead). It would be also possible to add rules that change the dimmer/color items when the switches receive a command, but I didn't do that.

[2017-07-13T13:39:16Z | calohmn | comment]
First thoughts:
The `io.vertx.core.net.impl.NetClientImpl` objects are still referenced in the `closeHooks` of the Vertx context.

To me it looks like there may be an issue in `io.vertx.proton.impl.ProtonClientImpl.connect()` / `connectNetClient()`.
The created `NetClient` instance is not closed there in case of a failed connection attempt. Thereby the instance is not removed from the Vertx context `closeHooks` and can't be garbage-collected.
If there is consensus on this explanation, we could file a vertx-proton issue for this.

I currently don't see a workaround in Hono. Letting the reconnects be handled by `NetClientImpl` (by using `protonClientOptions.setReconnectAttempts(-1)`) would undo the fix for #209.

[2017-07-14T07:50:33Z | sophokles73 | comment]
Your analysis looks very reasonable to me. I agree that invoking `NetclientImpl.close()` in the *failing* part of the connection handler in `ProtonClientImpl.connectNetClient()` should properly unregister the *closeHook* from the `Context` and prevent the memory leak.
Luckily, this seems not to be a problem when an existing connection fails as the underlying `ProtonTransport` will invoke `NetClient.close()` in this case.

> I currently don't see a workaround in Hono. Letting the reconnects be handled by NetClientImpl (by using protonClientOptions.setReconnectAttempts(-1)) would undo the fix for #209.

I also do not think that this would actually solve the problem because the `NetClient` is also not closed if the SASL handshake fails (e.g. due to incorrect credentials) :-(

Story...

PlatformIO handles dependencies when you install a library. It can be manual installation or specifying dependency in project file `platformio.ini`.  

Here we have 3-rd situation. Your library depends on a few other libs. It's OK and COOL. But... You use CI that doesn't handle dependency. You manually control which libraries to use and where they are located when call `pio ci...`. But... New PlatformIO 3.0 Build System is very smart. @RivaStyle @jebrando I could reproduce this issue. I suspect the problem is with `InitializeConnection` function in `iothubtransport_mqtt_common.c`. `InitializeConnection` does not handle all retry actions appropriately. 

I am adding some pain points in the `InitializeConnection` function, which I think causes the crash. _(Note: This is compared against master branch, latest commit 1239a17)_

**Line 2331** : [View Code](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/1239a173f7e590dc821bcbb243703bea2969ebc7/iothub_client/src/iothubtransport_mqtt_common.c#L2331)

I think `result = 0` is incorrect, and this is causing a crash when I add `IoTHubDeviceClient_LL_SetRetryPolicy(iotHubClientHandle, IOTHUB_CLIENT_RETRY_INTERVAL, 20)` in the application logic.

**RETRY_ACTION_RETRY_LATER retry action is not being handled**

When retry action is `RETRY_ACTION_RETRY_LATER`, the return value of `InitializeConnection` is `0`, which also results in crash. The return value when retry action is `RETRY_ACTION_RETRY_LATER` should be something other than `0`.

@jebrando Can you confirm whether this is true, and let me know if you would like me to raise a PR to resolve this issue. Thanks.

[2014-06-09T23:20:12Z | stewart | comment]
Looking into this more, it's actually _technically_ not a bug. What's happening is due to Node's event loop, by the time the event listeners are attached for the devices, the events have already been emitted, so we can't hook into them. The exception is for the last device, which emits the 'start' event on the same tick that the work block begins processing and sets up the handlers.

The devices are all going to be started by the time the work block begins running, so the device 'start' events are more or less worthless, and will be removed from both docs and code shortly.

I also had alignment traps on an arm. The memory access addresses in the trap messages showed the problem was in accessing the uip_buf buffer, more specificly in the UIP_IP_BUF part. I suspected it was an alignment problem of the UIP_IP_BUF uip_ip_hdr struct into the uip_buf array, tried increasing `UIP_CONF_LLH_LEN` to 16 and the alignment traps went away. 
Then I found this in `6lbr-conf-zoul.h`

```
// IP packet must be 4 bytes aligned
#undef UIP_CONF_LLH_LEN
#define UIP_CONF_LLH_LEN 16
```

Seems they had the same problem.
Well just increasing `UIP_CONF_LLH_LEN` is not ok, as the ethernet header read is in fact 14 and not 16 bytes, so I padded the `uip_eth_hdr` part of `uip_buf` with two bytes in the `eth_drv_input` function.
It seems I still have something to fix though, but the alignment traps went away.

[2018-07-10T18:08:00Z | darobs | comment]
Hello @chriswaters78 , @neumanndaniel,

We need to document this better, but if you set the Environment variable "OptimizeForPerformance" to "false" for the EdgeHub, all of our known OOM issues are resolved:

In the portal, this is set in a deployment by selecting "Configure advanced Edge Runtime settings, and adding an environment variable to Edge Hub.

In the deployment JSON, this would look like this:

```json
                    "edgeHub": {
                        "type": "docker",
                        "settings": {
                            "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/azureiotedge-hub:1.0",
                            "createOptions": "{\n  \"HostConfig\": {\n    \"PortBindings\": {\n      \"8883/tcp\": [\n        {\n          \"HostPort\": \"8883\"\n        }\n      ],\n      \"443/tcp\": [\n        {\n          \"HostPort\": \"443\"\n        }\n      ],\n      \"5671/tcp\": [\n        {\n          \"HostPort\": \"5671\"\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}"
                        },
                        "env": {
                            "OptimizeForPerformance": {
                                "value": "false"
                            }
                        },
                        "status": "running",
                        "restartPolicy": "always"
                    }
```

My edgeHub container has been running for 13 days today. If this doesn't solve your issues, we'll have to start a new investigation.

Updated:  
[We do have this documented in our Troubleshooting section.](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/iot-edge/troubleshoot#stability-issues-on-resource-constrained-devices)

[2019-12-06T20:27:03Z | mkellsy | comment]
@Doublenik8
I am assuming you can access the interface from **http://hoobs.local**. If you can't let me know.

## Environment
1. Download and install [https://www.getpostman.com/](https://www.getpostman.com/).
2. Open Postman and then click on the workspace dropdown. (Next to Invite) and then click on **Create New**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 12 55 16 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352170-c704e780-1827-11ea-869f-18d756c53147.png)
3. Set the name to **HOOBS** and click **Create Workspace**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 12 57 01 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352249-eef44b00-1827-11ea-9f42-525b73ea004d.png)
4. Make sure HOOBS is selected (You just created it, sometimes Postman doesn't automatically select it)
5. Download this from HOOBS [https://github.com/hoobs-org/HOOBS/raw/master/postman.zip](https://github.com/hoobs-org/HOOBS/raw/master/postman.zip) and un-zip it.
6. Click the Manage Environment button (it's the gear in the upper right).
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 00 14 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352488-793caf00-1828-11ea-934a-225679810bfe.png)
7. Click **Import**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 01 22 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352527-8fe30600-1828-11ea-9f57-f2a8aabe4b13.png)
8. Browse to the un-zipped file from HOOBS and select **enviornment.json**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 02 16 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352605-b7d26980-1828-11ea-9604-740e805ebe1e.png)
9. Clock on **hoobs.local**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 18 52 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353607-f9fcaa80-182a-11ea-8759-31d08d72de33.png)
10. Set the **username** and **password** fields. This will be the same username and password you use to log into HOOBS.
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 17 47 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353642-1567b580-182b-11ea-9f80-63ffa257f2fc.png)
11. Click **Update**
12. Now close the dialog (Not Add, use the X)
13. Now in the Environment drop-down, select **hoobs.local**.
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 04 16 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70352711-fcf69b80-1828-11ea-9e0d-c42fe598ee84.png)

## Commands
Now that you have the environment setup, you need to add the commands.
1. Click File -> Import
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 10 16 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353084-cbca9b00-1829-11ea-96a1-29773722c402.png)
2. Go to the **Import Folder** tab and then Click **Choose Folders** and select the **collections** folder. (this is from the zip file you downloaded from HOOBS)
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 29 10 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70354324-79d74480-182c-11ea-88d1-4ba55b3eb2c0.png)
3. You should see all of the commands now
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 13 30 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353257-3f6ca800-182a-11ea-9ce4-8e5260f5d89f.png)

## What I Actually Need
Now you can run commands against the HOOBS API.
1. Open **Authentication** and click on **Login**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 14 48 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353353-6aef9280-182a-11ea-8974-6dbe952e1425.png)
2. Click **Send**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 15 31 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353405-7fcc2600-182a-11ea-8532-0f8a0fea5405.png)
3. You will see this, but you don't need to do anything with it. It's just logging in.
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 23 43 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353948-b6567080-182b-11ea-8b69-4503be28f1de.png)
4. Now open **Accessories** and click on **List Accessories**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 24 34 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70353986-cff7b800-182b-11ea-8196-7fc8b3802401.png)
5. Now click **Send**
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 25 30 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70354033-e6057880-182b-11ea-9fa4-d837c16517a0.png)
6. You will see something like this.
![Screen Shot 2019-12-06 at 1 25 54 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9777975/70354065-f584c180-182b-11ea-9610-306f1b7ef38f.png)
7. Select all and paste the response into this task. That's the data I need to see what Accessory Roborock is reporting.

[2017-01-12T11:44:42Z | amitjoy | comment]
Yes, it has been kept unbounded intentionally. The events fired by WireEmitter instances are maintained here. There also exists consumer threads which consumes the data from this queue. So, we can make sure that for every data produced by the queue, there will be enough number of consumers to consume this data at the same time. There cannot be data producers without consumers or vice versa. And that's why the queue is unbounded.

[2017-01-12T13:48:44Z | ctron | comment]
The only consumer of this queue is the `doGet` method of the servlet.

So when Wire applications are running (in the background) they are producing events. Filling up the queue. So as long as no one keeps a Web UI open, Kura will OOM at some point. Is that the intention?

Beside that only one Web UI session will receive events. So the Web UI may only be used by a single user. Is that also intentionally.

[2017-01-12T14:07:31Z | amitjoy | comment]
The size of the `ConcurrentLinkedQueue` is unbounded and if producers are producing values faster than the consumers, it can indeed end up with OOM. It is definitely better to switch to bounded blocking queues to prevent OOM. Good catch 👍.

The limitation of one IP address per MAC address is indeed a limitation of the current neighbor table implementation of Contiki, even having both a link local and a global address should not be possible, but there is a loophole allowing this. This is an oversimplification that is perfectly fine for RPL network, but breaks when using more vanilla IPv6 configuration.

There is a workaround implemented in 6LBR, but it's rather limited. There is also a PR pending in Contiki about that topic, see https://github.com/contiki-os/contiki/pull/2098 , that should provide a more comprehensive fix, but I did not had time to look at it in depth yet. And I'm a bit reluctant to merge it into 6LBR blindly as it could stealthy break many things.

But if you're adventurous you could merge it and try if it solves your problem, in the mean time I will try to find some time to carefully review it.

[2018-02-14T09:20:18Z | sophokles73 | comment]
The reason for this seems to be missing quotation marks around the *version* label in the Kubernetes resource descriptors we use for deploying Grafana/influxDB. When the value is something like `0.5-M11` then Kubernetes is smart enough to determine that the value is a string. However, when the value is just `0.5` it tries to parse it as an integer and fails to do so.

[2018-02-16T07:49:55Z | sophokles73 | comment]
This problem can be circumvented quite easily.

If you are deploying using the binary archive downloaded from the [Download page](https://www.eclipse.org/hono/download/), do the following:
```shell
eclipse-hono-example-0.5$: sed -i.orig -e 's/version: *0.5/version: "0.5"/' deploy/kubernetes/*.yml
```
Then deploy using
```
eclipse-hono-example-0.5$: deploy/kubernetes/kubernetes_deploy.sh
```

If you are deploying from the source tree, do the following *before* you run the build:
```shell
HONO_HOME$: cd example
HONO_HOME/example$: sed -i.orig -e 's/version: *${project.version}/version: "${project.version}"/' src/main/deploy/kubernetes/*.yml
```

Then do the build and deploy to Kubernetes as described in the deployment guide.

I dont have access to my logs right now, but I was experiencing the same thing with both the LZW30-SN and LZW31-SN (I dont think config files for the LZW31-SN are not on github yet). Here is what I discovered:

- When OpenZwave 1.6 loads the config file the very first time, everything works except for scenes.
- If you restart z2m or use refresh note info, ozw appears to check for an updated config file online
- Ozw claims to find an updated config, so it renames the original config file to something like lzw31-sn.xml.1 and attempts to download the updated config

[2018-04-04T08:34:42Z | ctron | comment]
Ok, looking more closely the issue gets more complex. 

The exception is not coming from the call to `sync`, but to the combination of modifying the watchdog and a reboot being in progress. The call to sync took a while (as it might happen) and at the same time (not intentionally) I did disable the watchdog (which causes an update). Which then causes a call to `cancel` on the poll task, which was busy waiting for `sync` at the same time. So it is not the `sync` command which failed, but the Java task of waiting for the return. However `IOException` is treated the same as `InterruptedException`.

So I think there are a few things to fix here:

1. A failed call to `sync` should not prevent a reboot
1. The shutdown of the watchdog should not cancel the task with `mayInterruptIfRunning` set to `true`. If the reboot is in progress then it should continue.
1. I think the poll task could be left alone if the ping interval didn't change
1. Also the logic of the `performWatchdogActions` seems a little bit odd to me. Maybe this is again designed that way and I simply don't understand it. But if the watchdog should be stopped (`watchdogToStop = true`) and the call gets executed again (like in this scenario), then the watchdog is refreshed. I do understand that the HW watchdog should be kept alive as long as the "sync" is running. But in the cause either "sync" or "reboot" fail, the watchdog should not be refreshed any longer. So in case of any exception to one of those two calls, refreshing the watchdog should stop IMHO.

[2016-08-15T13:06:06Z | danchom | review_comment]
In all other places (other handlers) there is not a colon (Please see handlers map of BaseModuleHandlerFactory. I don't know why, may be to have less string concatenations). In all these places  ruleId + moduleId is unique  identifier of the handler. 
The RuleEngine has a mapping between module type and list of rules where the module type is  used. (In that way it changes rule state not_initialized <-> initialized) 
A rule which have composite module type depends on its all child module types. There for the composite module type has to update Rule Engine's module type to rule mapping. 
The colon is used to separate rule id from the rest of prefix, because if you have a nested composite module types (i.e. ItemStateChangeTrigger) the method is called in recursion and rule id will be loosed. For that reason the composite module type uses colon in definition of unique id of handler.

`appdaemon.plugins.hass.hassapi` is the full path to the `hassapi` module within the `hass` package. `Hass` is a class within the `hassapi` module. "Parts" and "sub-parts" are not nomenclature used in Python.

There are multiple ways to import and use that class. This:

```python
from appdaemon.plugins.hass.hassapi import Hass
class test(Hass):
```

import appdaemon.plugins.hass.hassapi as hass
class test(hass.Hass):

[2018-03-23T21:10:36Z | jspaith | comment]
First thanks to everyone for repro steps & my apologies that this has lingered so long.

**;tl-dr.  We have a provisional fix, look for it sometime next week.  It will make the 3/30 release.**

Because I'm guessing the audience here is geeks and wants the details...

MQTT_WS on reconnection is not properly blasting the tlsio_* layer and there's cached gunk lying around that we pass to openssl, schannel (this repros on Windows).  AMQP_WS in fact does clean up after itself which is why this bug doesn't repro on it.

I've put in a proof of concept in MQTT where its much more aggressive cleaning up its lower layer.  It's working very well in smoke tests; I've killed proxy ~10 times across varying lengths of timeouts and MQTT_WS always returns.  On both Windows 10 and Ubuntu 16.04.

Even though this is like a 2 liner and even though we have auto-fault injection tests that run on the gate (for non-proxies) which in theory would catch regressions, changes like this are going to get additional human review of change itself.  We're also going to see if other places have this class of bug.  So sometime next week is our timeline.

https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/compare/mqtt-ws-proxy has wave 1 of the fix; it's not the final (there's false positive error messages and it may make sense to break this function up instead of the if checks).

```
Shared Subscriptions

With support of shared subscriptions, Client Load Balancing is now included in MQTT. The message load of a single topic is distributed amongst all subscribers (this was already supported by HiveMQ for MQTT 3.1 & MQTT 3.1.1).

A Shared Subscription is identified using a special style of Topic Filter.

The format of this filter is:

$share/{ShareName}/{filter} 

$share – is a literal string that marks the Topic Filter as being a Shared Subscription Topic
{ShareName} – is a character string that does not include “/”, “+” or “#”
{filter} – is the remainder of the string has the same syntax and semantics as a Topic Filter in a non-shared subscription.

[2018-03-05T22:28:49Z | ewertons | comment]
Starting on OS X El Capitan, Mac OS comes with SIP (System Integrity Protection) which blocks brew from installing/creating links over the existing paths on /usr/* (https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT204899)
After installing curl with brew and forcing link creations (into /usr/local/*), cmake is able to recognize the keg version of curl installed.
However since the original curl libraries are not overwritten (under /usr/lib), the application will still find the old libcurl.4.dylib (on High Sierra, 7.54.0) and use it, reproducing the bug described in this issue.
To complete the workaround one must set DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH.

I believe that the AFNetworking version used a connection per request so was able to parallelize the requests more and may have resulted in faster loading in some situations.  

Round-trip latency to the server could play a big part here and a higher connection pool count would likely speed things up. @htreu Could you have a look? I agree with @hsudbrock that there should be no dependency on the processing order.

[2017-11-07T11:32:48Z | htreu | comment]
Yes, agreed. The processing order should not change the result here.
Since we want .cfg files with an exclusive PID marker (like `pid:my.service.pid` in the first line) to be really exclusive and especially benefit from the file delete mechanism we should drop all other entries with this pid from other files. So when a file later defines a key/value pair for an already known exclusive PID (e.g. by defining the pid inline like `my.service.pid:key=value`) this line will be skipped.

The only order dependent processing is then given for .cfg files which define the same exclusive pid in the first line: here the file processed last will win and have its values passed to the configAdmin. A warning will be logged about the subsequent definition of an exclusive PID.

[2017-01-16T15:31:45Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
Now this is nasty. @aounhaider1 found out that this is due to the ConfigDescriptionParameterDTO - as "default" is a reserved keyword in Java, the DTO uses "defaultValue" as a field name instead of "default". Therefore, the serialized JSON becomes "defaultValue", although our XMLs contain "default". I think the right thing to do is to add a `@SerializedName("default")` to the field.
But this means that it is a breaking change - any UIs that currently expect "defaultValue" will need to be adapted...

Any thoughts, @maggu2810 & @sjka?

[2017-01-16T19:52:57Z | maggu2810 | comment]
I am fine with both.
Is there any need that the DTO for the REST interface uses the same name as the XML element or only to keep one wording if possible?

[2017-01-17T12:19:10Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> Is there any need that the DTO for the REST interface uses the same name as the XML element or only to keep one wording if possible?

What needs to be the same are the property names within the XML and the JSON - because both refer to the same [definition of config descriptions](https://www.eclipse.org/smarthome/documentation/development/bindings/xml-reference.html#configuration-descriptions) (which we actually should also update to also embrace JSON). The internal field name of the DTO can be different, but the input and output should match. Note that we also ask developers to define config descriptions in JSON (for the automation component), therefore we cannot chose a different name on the REST API - that would be a mess.

[2017-03-20T15:11:20Z | pierantoniomerlino | comment]
I fixed the issue regarding the GPS static position. 

However, there are a couple of issues that we have to address:
1. Each time the modem monitor fires, it emits a GPS device present event. This triggers the position service and a birth certificate is published. So, if the "republish.mqtt.birth.cert.on.gps.lock" property is set, at every monitor run a birth message is published. As a result, a lot of birth messages are publish even if the static position is enabled.
2. If the GPS device is not present, the last acquired position is published.

For the first item, IMHO we should publish the first birth message and filter the others when a static position is set. For the latter, it makes sense to publish the last acquired position and at least log that the GPS device is not present.

@ctron @cdealti what do you think?

Just to understand, what is the benefit of doing it that way, instead of using the Debian package manager?

[2016-08-22T13:09:52Z | dwoodard1 | comment]
For systems that may not have package managers installed. To keep the build uniform, we create install scripts for all platforms (RPi, BBB, Intel Edison, etc.). For systems that typically have support for easily installing from DEB files (RPi, BBB), we wrap the installer in a DEB package. For those that don't (Edison), we just distribute the installer. 

This is mostly a historical artifact. The Debian packages were created shortly after the release of Kura. The script installers were in existence long before Kura released. There may be a better way of managing these, we just haven't seen it as a priority to modify the build.

@shbatm @JasonSwindle What I suggest is to do like @shbatm said because if I update to fix this I would break every lock on older versions of hass.

The options to fix this are

1) Edit the main lock configuration [here](https://github.com/OpenZWave/Zwave2Mqtt/blob/master/hass/configurations.js#L366) by just add:

```js
'lock': {
    type: 'lock',
    object_id: 'lock',
    discovery_payload: {
      command_topic: true,
      payload_lock: 'true',
      payload_unlock: 'false',
     state_locked: true, // PROPERTY TO ADD
     state_unlocked: false, // PROPERTY TO ADD
      value_template: '{% if value_json.value == false %} false {% elif value_json.value == true %} true {% else %} unknown {% endif %}'
    }
  },
```

This would fix all the locks of all your devices.

2) Fix each single lock device from control panel. Just select a node from the table than go in node tab under the table and scroll to `Hass devices` section, here fix the lock device by adding the 2 property previously shown than press on store to make this discovery payloads persistent

3) Check the device id of your lock devices and add a configuration in custom_devices.json for those devices. Check readme for more info

4) Open an issue on hass to make those lock properties not required in payload with some default values so this would work as before

[2018-01-22T18:28:22Z | Lakitna | comment]
@lwis noted that the value of the `5750` is different. I've done a little digging and here is what I found:

From const.py:
```
ATTR_APPLICATION_TYPE = "5750"
```

So it should denote something like the purpose of the device. After printing the raw output of all my devices (not just lights) I found that `5750` can have a few different values:

0 = Remote control
1 = ??? I think dimmer remote, but I don't have any so I can't check
2 = Light bulb or panel
3 = ??? Or maybe this is the dimmer remote? 
4 = Motion sensor

With @mhlund his lamp `5750` is 0, suggesting that it's a remote control in the eyes of the Gateway. Like all other devices with `5750` = 0 it uses `15009` to store it's values. Light bulbs (`5750` = 2) do this in `3311`.

In conclusion. Somehow the Gateway of @mhlund thinks that his lamps are remote controls. I suggest repairing, that might repair the issue.

edit: For those who are interested in that sort of thing, you can find the raw output of all possible devices you can connect to a tradfri network and that I have access to here: https://gist.github.com/Lakitna/b6b041410431bcedff67a947640fb281

[2018-01-23T11:32:58Z | Lakitna | comment]
So in conclusion: Somehow there was a problem in the pairing process resulting the GU10 bulbs to be recognised as remotes. This resulted in the original error. The solution was to reset the Gateway and re-pair the network. This problem can be identified by looking at the `5750` key, this has a value of `2` when identified as a lamp and `0` when identified as a remote.

While figuring this out @ggravlingen and @lwis made a fix. That fix is now only worth something as a fallback for when this issue appears again.

The IKEA app identifies devices differently than Pytradfri does. IKEA doesn't seem to rely on the value of `5750` at all or on `3311` being present. Instead, the app probably looks at the presence of any lamp values (ex: Lamp state, dimmer value etc.). A curious choice when `5750` exists.

We can automate the detection of this issue, that might be a good addition to the examples or wiki.

[2017-08-01T08:37:17Z | htreu | comment]
I guess the main thing here is the line `scanner.useDelimiter("\\A").next()` which was technically not clear to me either but I must admit I did take the exact same line from stackoverflow in the past to convert InputStreams to Strings. I did a little research and found this article: https://community.oracle.com/blogs/pat/2004/10/23/stupid-scanner-tricks

The line effectively takes the whole content of the InputStream and reads it into the String. The \A refers to the beginning of the Stream. So the Scanner will tokenize the whole Stream until it reaches the next beginning (which is not present here) resulting in the whole string being taken as the first token.

With this in mind I guess its fine to replace the method. Its only called once in the HttpClient in the hue binding.

On another note: We should replace the internal HttpClient from the hue binding by the jetty client (or even better by the `org.eclipse.smarthome.io.net.http.HttpUtil`) but thats another PR with some more analysis :-)

@jeroenhansen I have fixed the issue so that if you specify an empty Metadata object {}, the existing metadata will not be wiped out.  This way, you can have a listener on metadata changes.

[2016-12-15T18:45:21Z | Propanu | comment]
New version is up on NPM, 1.0.2-src. I've tracked the issue and found out it was caused by the makefile template node-gyp uses to build the sources. The target rules only use the base filename, thus if you have both a *module.c* and *module.cxx* in the same package, one of them will not be included in the build.

Since I doubt this can be fixed quickly by the node-gyp guys, I decided to rename our C sources while packing them in order to fix this. Everything seems to work as intended now.

[2017-08-29T11:57:48Z | kjasdal | comment]
Seeing that this has gotten a "bug"-label, I just wanted to summarize what I believe are issues that should be looked at (and hopefully corrected):

1) When the DailyJob is run at midnight, the Sun Phase state is set to UNDEF. 
- This should not happen (the state should continue to be NIGHT).
2) There is a Sun Phase called NOON that seems to have a duration of one minute (although some comment in the code states that NOON has the same start and end time). 
- NOON should not be a Sun Phase since this is a specific point in time, and not a duration.
- It makes sense to keep it as an Event, though. 
- If it is difficult implementation-wise to have one and not the other, I guess NOON could be kept with a duration of 0 minutes. 
- In this case, the DAYLIGHT period needs to be split into two periods; one before NOON and one after NOON, to be able to move back to DAYLIGHT after passing NOON. As it is now, NOON continues all the way until SUNSET, :-)

> it no longer allows you to programmatically set all elements of a HSBK value

Imho it is fully ok with dropping that "feature" as I fully agree with the comment from LIFX:
_"We went with kelvin also setting saturation to 0 as we felt it covers the most common use case where people would want the light to be set to white when they set kelvin."_

Actually, I doubt that setting a Kelvin value for any color (but white) makes any kind of sense...
So the color temperature channel should always set the saturation to 0.

> So I currently use this in some presets where the tint of the K value makes or breaks how nice (warm) the light is.

You just have to choose another hue/saturation combination to reach exactly the same goal. There isn't such a thing as HSBK, this is an (unduly) invention by LIFX.

> would also like to use custom fade times from within rules. Any ideas on how that could be accomplished?

I do not want to go into this - ESH does not support parameterized commands, this would lead us to RPC-style communication with a lot additional complexity. [2018-01-31T07:42:52Z | technobly | comment]
The original spec for AUTOMATIC, SEMI_AUTOMATIC and MANUAL is here:
https://github.com/particle-iot/firmware/issues/216

Particle.connect() in SEMI_AUTOMATIC and SINGLE-THREADED mode was always designed to be a blocking call.

---

Now that we have MULTI-THREADED mode, can we not just use that for unblocking things and let SINGLE-THREADED mode be mostly blocking as it was originally intended to be?

---

>why on earth would loop() need to be prevented from running again till connected.

Here are some thoughts, it's not as simple as just running loop() because loop() is most important.  In the single-threaded world, If we are supposed to be connected to the Cloud, and are not yet, that Cloud connection needs to be established and there is work to be done.  Wi-Fi must be connected, and the Cloud handshake needs to occur.  After that we maintain a heartbeat every ~15s but also process any incoming/outgoing messages every time loop() ends.  If we go off and run loop() before those initial things happen, we could be taking a very long time to connect to the Cloud depending on what's happening in loop().  This is however the entire reason for multi-threaded mode, so loop() can run while all of those background activities are blocking and doing their thing.

Are you aware that the IoTHubClient has a feature called Retry Policy? The default retry policy is EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF_WITH_JITTER. It means that if there is a disconnection, the client will retry connecting within 1 second, then 2 secs, 4, 8, ... eventually taking a long time (hours) if the connection has been disrupted for too long. 
The exponential retry policy is not recommended for connections that stay offline for too long (several minutes). 

You can control the retry policy by using this [API function](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/master/iothub_client/inc/iothub_client_ll.h#L375).

> This continues until a result resource bundle is instantiated or the list of candidate bundle names is exhausted. If no matching resource bundle is found, the default control's getFallbackLocale method is called, which returns the current default locale.
